class_guess: Bouncer + Chaotic Edge (edge erodes the bouncer block; golden-mean invariant)
summary: Bouncer; chaotic left edge slowly eats the 1-block. No-00 invariant: it can only halt if the edge eats the whole block
mechanism: Bouncer: a solid 1-block gains one 1 per bounce; left of it sits a chaotic, aperiodic edge (~0.6 bits/cell).
Each bounce C dives into the edge in zigzag waves; the edge eats ~0.06 block cells per bounce on average, up to 11.
No 00 ever lies between head and rightmost 1 (checked to 1e9, local proof): it halts only if the block falls to 2 cells.

rules.name: Wave turns at 00
rules.cases: C on 0 with a 0 to its left

rules.name: Wave carry 010
rules.cases: C on 0, left cells 0 1; wave continues

rules.name: Wave fold 110
rules.cases: C on 0, left cells 1 1 (with the two rules above: complete split of C on 0)

rules.name: Bounce map (block = wall)
rules.cases: n >= e(w)+3; f, e, s from the wall model (does not depend on n); also exact on 32,061 consecutive real bounces

rules.name: Halting door (only way to halt)
rules.cases: j >= 0; the only path into E0 is A0, B1, F0^j, F1, D0 (traced back from the transition table)

rules.name: No 00 right of head (invariant)
rules.cases: Only B0 moves left writing 0, and its right neighbour is always 1. Validated at every step; arbitrary-left search: 182,877 states, 0 violations

rules.name: End doors (door + invariant)
rules.cases: with the invariant these are the only halting configurations: the block has been eaten down to 2 cells

template.diff: 8 of 11 transitions differ (best mirror+relabel); InfiniteRect_v1 TM4: 8; LongNv1 TM1/TM2: 9
template.note: Bouncer_v3 needs a periodic side (RC i -> RC (i+1) every 128 bounces). Here 300/300 snapshots have distinct skeletons, and the mirrored RC 0 does not reach RC 1 after 128 bounces. LongN and InfiniteRect also need periodic interaction streams.

strategy: 1) Prove the no-00 invariant as a closed predicate on the right side (progress_nonhalt_cond; checks the 11 transitions). Then halting needs A> 0 11 0^inf or A> 0 101 0^inf. 2) Show the edge never eats the block below 3 cells. This needs a potential that bounds the edge's growth per bounce (open). 3) Get from the blank tape to bounce ~30 (n=29) with es/execute, then apply 1) and 2) with an arbitrary left side l.
risks: The crux is a bound on erosion, and the edge's growth looks statistical: 0.057/bounce on average, up to 11 in one bounce, 60 in 50 bounces. If there is no deterministic bound, the machine is cryptid-like.
There was an early close call: the block was 2 cells long at bounces 10 and 14-16. The init phase must simulate past it.
Twin #26 `1RB1RA_1LC1RE_---0LD_1LE1LD_0RA0LF_1LF0LB` differs in 6 transitions, so we must re-derive the invariant before claiming 2 kills.

checkpoint_questions.text: Fig 1: the stripes on the left are frozen; only the textured fringe at the white block keeps changing. Agree the fringe is the only part to bound?
Fig 2: between the head and the white block, are there never two black (0) cells side by side?
Fig 3: in the bottom-left panel, does the erosion per bounce look like noise with no pattern a proof could use? That is why it is flagged cryptid-like.
